question: Assign seven staff members (Person 0 to Person 6) to three projects (Project 0, Project 1, and Project 2) such that each staff member is assigned to exactly one project. Each project has specific skill requirements: Project 0 requires a skill level of 8 for Skill 0 and 8 for Skill 1, Project 1 requires a skill level of 7 for Skill 0 and 9 for Skill 1, and Project 2 requires a skill level of 9 for Skill 0 and 7 for Skill 1. Each staff member has specific skill levels: Person 0 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 1 has Skill 0 level 6 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 2 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 3 has Skill 0 level 6 and Skill 1 level 7, Person 4 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 6, Person 5 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 6, and Person 6 has Skill 0 level 5 and Skill 1 level 7. The attained skill level for each project is the sum of the skill levels of the assigned staff members. The skill shortage for each project is the difference between the required skill level and the attained skill level. The goal is to minimize the maximum skill shortage across all projects and skills. Constraints include ensuring that each staff member is assigned to exactly one project, and that the skill shortages for Project 0, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -8, for Project 0, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -8, for Project 1, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -7, for Project 1, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -9, for Project 2, Skill 0 must be less than or equal to -9, and for Project 2, Skill 1 must be less than or equal to -7.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "persons": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "projects": [0, 1, 2],
    "skills": [0, 1],
    # skill[p, s]
    "person_skill": {
        (0, 0): 5, (0, 1): 7,
        (1, 0): 6, (1, 1): 7,
        (2, 0): 5, (2, 1): 7,
        (3, 0): 6, (3, 1): 7,
        (4, 0): 5, (4, 1): 6,
        (5, 0): 5, (5, 1): 6,
        (6, 0): 5, (6, 1): 7,
    },
    # required[j, s]
    "requirement": {
        (0, 0): 8, (0, 1): 8,
        (1, 0): 7, (1, 1): 9,
        (2, 0): 9, (2, 1): 7,
    },
    # shortage upper bounds short[j, s] <= bound
    "short_maxbound": {
        (0, 0): -8, (0, 1): -8,
        (1, 0): -7, (1, 1): -9,
        (2, 0): -9, (2, 1): -7,
    },
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    persons = d["persons"]
    projects = d["projects"]
    skills = d["skills"]
    pairs_js = [(j, s) for j in projects for s in skills]

    m.Persons = pyo.Set(initialize=persons)
    m.Projects = pyo.Set(initialize=projects)
    m.Skills = pyo.Set(initialize=skills, ordered=True)
    m.PairJS = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs_js, dimen=2)

    # ---------- decision variables ----------
    # x[p, j] = 1 if person p assigned to project j
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.Persons, m.Projects, within=pyo.Binary)
    # short[j, s] = attained[j,s] - required[j,s]
    m.short = pyo.Var(m.PairJS, within=pyo.Reals)
    # z = max shortage across all (j, s)
    m.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Reals)

    # ---------- objective ----------
    # minimize the maximum skill shortage across all projects and skills
    def obj_rule(m):
        return m.z
    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---------- constraints ----------
    # (1) each person assigned to exactly one project
    def assign_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.x[p, j] for j in m.Projects) == 1
    m.assign = pyo.Constraint(m.Persons, rule=assign_rule)

    # (2) shortage definition: short[j,s] = sum_p skill[p,s]*x[p,j] - required[j,s]
    def short_def_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.short[j, s] == sum(
            d["person_skill"][(p, s)] * m.x[p, j] for p in m.Persons
        ) - d["requirement"][(j, s)]
    m.short_def = pyo.Constraint(m.PairJS, rule=short_def_rule)

    # (3) shortage upper bounds from problem statement
    def short_bound_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.short[j, s] <= d["short_maxbound"][(j, s)]
    m.short_bound = pyo.Constraint(m.PairJS, rule=short_bound_rule)

    # (4) min-max linearisation: z >= short[j,s] for all (j,s)
    def z_rule(m, j, s):
        return m.z >= m.short[j, s]
    m.z_ge_short = pyo.Constraint(m.PairJS, rule=z_rule)

    return m

# SETS
#   PEOPLE   = {0,...,6}   seven staff members
#   PROJECTS = {0,1,2}     three projects
#   SKILLS   = {0,1}       two skills
#
# DECISION VARIABLES

#   short[j, k] in Reals   shortage for project j, skill k
#                          = required[j,k] - attained[j,k]
#   z        in Reals      maximum shortage across all (project, skill) pairs
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize)
#   minimize z  (the maximum skill shortage over all projects and skills)
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   (1) Each person assigned to exactly one project:
#         sum_j x[p,j] = 1   for all p
#   (2) Shortage definition for each (project, skill):
#         short[j,k] = required[j,k] - sum_p skill[p,k] * x[p,j]
#   (3) z dominates every shortage:
#         z >= short[j,k]   for all j,k
#   (4) Source-sentence bounds on shortages:
#         short[0,0] <= -8, short[0,1] <= -8,
#         short[1,0] <= -7, short[1,1] <= -9,
#         short[2,0] <= -9, short[2,1] <= -7
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "PEOPLE": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "PROJECTS": [0, 1, 2],
    "SKILLS": [0, 1],
    # skill[p][k] : skill level of person p in skill k
    "skill": {
        (0, 0): 5, (0, 1): 7,
        (1, 0): 6, (1, 1): 7,
        (2, 0): 5, (2, 1): 7,
        (3, 0): 6, (3, 1): 7,
        (4, 0): 5, (4, 1): 6,
        (5, 0): 5, (5, 1): 6,
        (6, 0): 5, (6, 1): 7,
    },
    # required[j][k] : required skill level for project j, skill k
    "required": {
        (0, 0): 8, (0, 1): 8,
        (1, 0): 7, (1, 1): 9,
        (2, 0): 9, (2, 1): 7,
    },
    # upper bounds on shortage per (project, skill) from the source sentences
    "shortage_ub": {
        (0, 0): -8, (0, 1): -8,
        (1, 0): -7, (1, 1): -9,
        (2, 0): -9, (2, 1): -7,
    },
    # big-M for shortage variable bounds
    "M": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.PEOPLE = pyo.Set(initialize=d["PEOPLE"])
    model.PROJECTS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["PROJECTS"])
    model.SKILLS = pyo.Set(initialize=d["SKILLS"])
    model.PS = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(j, k) for j in d["PROJECTS"] for k in d["SKILLS"]]
    )

    # Decision variables
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.PEOPLE, model.PROJECTS, within=pyo.Binary
    )
    model.short = pyo.Var(
        model.PS,
        within=pyo.Reals,
        bounds=(-d["M"], d["M"]),
    )
    model.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.Reals, bounds=(-d["M"], d["M"]))

    # (1) Each person assigned to exactly one project
    def person_rule(m, p):
        return sum(m.x[p, j] for j in m.PROJECTS) == 1

    model.person_assign = pyo.Constraint(model.PEOPLE, rule=person_rule)

    # (2) Shortage definition
    def shortage_rule(m, j, k):
        attained = sum(
            d["skill"][(p, k)] * m.x[p, j] for p in m.PEOPLE
        )
        return m.short[j, k] == d["required"][(j, k)] - attained

    model.shortage_def = pyo.Constraint(model.PS, rule=shortage_rule)

    # (3) z dominates every shortage
    def z_rule(m, j, k):
        return m.z >= m.short[j, k]

    model.z_dom = pyo.Constraint(model.PS, rule=z_rule)

    # (4) Source-sentence upper bounds on shortages
    def ub_rule(m, j, k):
        return m.short[j, k] <= d["shortage_ub"][(j, k)]

    model.shortage_ub = pyo.Constraint(model.PS, rule=ub_rule)

    # Objective: minimize the maximum shortage
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.z, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model
